findings.where: u4f-brief.md 2.2 :302 ("at most 2 a step ... a target more than 2 ahead leaves the stamps between unused"), :307 ("so no tick goes without a stamped command but by loss"); U4F-Q7 (iii) (c) :1300-1302; f36 :606; model N/u4f-r3/r2/p3_jumps.py; l1/src/lib.rs:146, :173, :190-192; results/u4r/0f066338dd8d/P3/runs.txt:18-20
findings.summary: TE3-1's fix holds under U4F-Q7 (b) but not under Q7 (a), which the brief still offers. Under (a) the target is newest + L, so it moves only as the newest tick moves. My model of P3 as L1 has it (3 seeds x 300,000 ticks, the 1 % adjacent swaps included) gives 21.2 % of steps with no newest move, against U4r's measured 17.7-20.3 %, so the model holds. In it the newest moves 3 or more in 1.16 % of steps. Under the words "leaves the stamps between unused", 1.22 % of ticks then get no stamped command, against -20's 0.1 % missing (marks.json:4724-4737). That fails on a correct build, and no lead fixes it, so f36 stops the build. The same words also skip stamps whenever a (b) controller's margin step, or a ClockSync correction, moves the target 3 or more at once. If owed stamps are carried at 2 a step instead, none is unused (largest backlog 3).
findings.fix: Replace the clause in 2.2 :302 with a catch-up rule: "a target more than 2 ahead is reached 2 a step, the owed stamps carried (none unused), while it is at most REDUNDANCY_CAP ahead of the previous stamp; only beyond that (a ClockSync reset) are the stamps between left unused, counted in stamps_skipped". Add: the controller moves its lead by at most 1 a step. Say stamps_skipped is expected to be 0 in every measured window. Have f36 assert stamps_skipped at most 0.1 % of ticks on its P3 trace, under Q7 (a) and (b) both while Q7 is open. If the skip is kept instead, tie Q7 (iii) (c) to Q7 (b), and say that (a) with (c) leaves about 1.2 % of P3's ticks unstamped.

findings.summary: 5.3 runs no twin, so the forged and clamp parts' twin checks find no params.twin. twin_of then returns a Gap (figures.rs:104-108), and a Gap makes the run invalid (eval.rs:346-347). On a correct build that means: p1's new bar "the twin check passing" cannot be met, and p1, p2, p7 and p8 all fail the rule "every check but the length-failing ones above passes on both". The bites also fail other checks by design. not-older-than (p9) fails the fast clock's movement check too (:5038-5049), and redundancy-1 (p12) fails the missing check too (:4724-4737). As worded, each of these sends a correct build to the advisor. Two wording problems as well: "the same" in p2-p6 now carries p1's forged and twin bars, and p13 (expected to pass) contradicts the rule that the named check fails on the bitten run.
findings.fix: List the forged and clamp twin checks beside the length-failing ones, as "no twin in 5.3: a Gap; the run is read by name, its validity apart from that Gap". Drop p1's "and the twin check passing", unless twin runs for p1 and p2 are added (+2 runs, with 5.5's pre-run disk and the counts changed to match). Word the rule per run: on a clean partner, every check but the length-failing and twin ones passes; on a bitten run, the named check fails and the checks its bite reaches may also fail (p9: the movement check; p12: the missing check). Spell p2-p6's "the same" as "every PM-0001-2 check passing and the shot band". Name p13 as the one bitten run whose check is expected to pass. Put the same words in D12.

findings.where: u4f-brief.md 5.3 p19 :908; U4F-Q15 (c) :1423-1424; 2.3 :315 and 2.4 item 3 :340-342 (W after kind 2, before kind 10); 2.6 lag switch :445; server/src/pump.rs:20, :84; l1/src/lib.rs:182-184
findings.summary: At P1 (25 ms +/- 5 ms each way, lead about 3), the burst from a 400 ms hold reaches the tick about 13 ticks after the first held command was given. The oldest 3 or 4 of the 12 commands are then 9 to 12 ticks past their stamps. Under U4F-Q18 (a) they are dropped as late before the catch-up cap. Separately, the Input bucket lets about 8 of the 12 datagrams through at once (pump.rs:20, :84), so at most 8 new commands ever reach the burst tick; the rest ride the next Input. On a correct build the cap therefore refuses nothing, and lagswitch_cmds_count peaks at about 5. So p19's "the catch-up cap refuses the excess, max 8" cannot hold, and Q15 (c)'s reason ("the cap shown acting on a hold that can exceed it") is wrong under the recommended Q18 (a). Without W, the max of 8 holds but the cap still refuses nothing, because of the bucket. The judged 200 ms parts and p13 are unchanged: their oldest command is about 4-5 ticks old, inside W.
findings.fix: Reword p19 to report, each counted apart: the commands dropped late by W, the input_limited datagrams and the kind-10 refusals, plus lagswitch_cmds_count's max (at most 8), with the arithmetic at P1. State that a hold sent through the honest endpoint can never put more than 8 new commands into one tick, because the bucket and W act first. Restate Q15 (c)'s why to match. If the cap must be seen acting, use kind 10's pattern: a sender putting more than 8 new commands, stamped inside [t - W, t + bound], into two datagrams in one tick. The forged suite already has it.

findings.where: u4f-brief.md 2.3 :316 and 2.4 item 4 :343-345 (join anchor); 2.2 :302, :307 (controller command rule); f13 (iii) :583; client/src/lib.rs:429; bots/src/lib.rs:14-16, :220-223; room/src/room.rs:681; ops/runs/c-u4r-r2.mjs:64-65
findings.summary: As built, no honest bots command can be stamped at or before the join tick. The bots give none until the endpoint holds a snapshot (bots/src/lib.rs:14-16, :221-223), and the first snapshot is of a tick at or after JoinAccepted's next_tick (room.rs:681), so newest + lead is at least join + 1. Rev 3.1's controller rule (2.2 :302, :307) replaces that rule for controller runs with "the commands the endpoint says are due". It does not restate "none until a snapshot" (nor "none until an estimate" under Q7 (b)), and it gives no first stamp, since there is no previous stamp yet. The endpoint still stamps a pre-snapshot command newest.map_or(0, ...) = 0 (:429). Lab runs start at --tick-start 63,736 (c-u4r-r2.mjs:64-65), so such a stamp lies far before any join tick: a kind-2 refusal on an honest client, against 2.5's "0 expected on honest clients". f13 (iii) tests only far-past first stamps (join - 1,000 and join - 2^31 + 1), so an off-by-one (refusing join + 1, or accepting a stamp equal to the join tick) passes it.
findings.fix: In 2.2, state: no command is due before the endpoint holds a snapshot (under Q7 (b), also a ClockSync estimate); the first command under the controller is stamped at the controller's target, never counted up from 0 or from the join tick; the endpoint's map_or(0) path cannot be reached under the controller, shown by a client test in which a command offered before the first snapshot is not stamped. Add to f13 (iii), under both options: a first stamp equal to the join tick refused as kind 2, and a first stamp of join + 1 accepted and run. State the test delta if these become new tests.

findings.summary: f16's 24 pairs run at 16 clients with a 2 s warm-up and 4 s measured. Nothing in 2.10 or f16 requires a pair to carry at least one forged item of its kind inside that window. The forgers forge every k-th command (kind 10 forges one episode after 8 held steps) at the rate the judged runs need: 1,000 per kind in 600 s is about one kind-10 episode every 4.8 s. So a pair can hold no forgery and still pass f16's equal-hash and equal-fate comparisons, comparing an honest run with an honest twin. Likewise f29, at 16 slots and 32 connects (two rounds, about 5 s), cannot come near carry 75's bound (about 30 s of events). Its "no admission refused" proves NA-16 only through Q4 (b)'s "no event stamped"; under Q4 (a) or (c) it proves nothing.
findings.fix: f16: each pair asserts its forger's sent_count for its kind is at least 1 inside the measured window (kind 10: one whole episode; the clamp: one beyond-reach point), and that the twin's matching datagram is present. Make the forging rate a lab setting at the short scale, as --connects is. f29: under Q4 (a) or (c), also assert the run's events per round against 32,768 / 21 (the arithmetic), or run the 1,000 connects once in the builder's D7 runs.

findings.where: u4f-brief.md 5.3 p20 :909; U4F-Q18 (a) :1471 ("f38 and p20 show it"); U4F-Q11 (v) (b) :1365-1367; SERIES.md:155
findings.summary: Under Q11 (v) (b), the idled fast client's stamps run on from previous + 1. After its 60 s idle they start about 1,800 ticks behind and close at 0.5 a tick (1.5 commands a tick, +1 each). So every command of p20's episode is dropped as late, and the excess (commands run minus server ticks and bound) is about -1,800. "Excess at most W" then holds for any W below about 900. It fails only if there is no W at all, so p20 cannot show the window's size. f38 does pin it (W + bound), so the evidence for Q18 (a) rests on f38 alone.
findings.fix: Either have p20's client resume by f38's pattern (8 commands a tick from its last stamp + 1, inside the bucket) and read excess at most W, with late > 0; or reword p20 as "every command of the episode dropped late; excess at most 0" and change Q18 (a)'s "f38 and p20 show it" to "f38 shows it; p20 shows the window closing an idled fast clock".

findings.where: u4f-brief.md 2.6 per-kind table, kind 1 :427, kind 3 :432; f15 :585
findings.summary: Kind 1's forged tick, "the lead bound plus 1 to 100 ticks ahead", names no reference. At P0, newest + bound + 1 equals the next tick to run plus the bound, which kind 1 accepts, so the low end of the range is not forged. Kind 3 adds "one older copy" of s-1. If the honest Input already carries s-1 unacknowledged, an added copy breaks codec rule (1) (NotCanonical, proto/src/input.rs:155-157), so the copy must replace it instead. f15's encode assert would catch both, but only as a builder stop.
findings.fix: Kind 1: "its newest command's tick set to the honest stamp plus the lead bound plus 1 to 100". Kind 3: "plus one older copy of s-1 with changed content; if s-1 already rides in the honest Input, that copy's content is changed in place".

summary:
**Verdict: PASS WITH FINDINGS. In my own scale that is REVISE.** No Critical or High is open. There are 5 Mediums and 6 Lows, all in rev 3.1's own changes. Every rev 3.1 line I name below was checked against the code at the head; spikes/ is unchanged between the two commits. I built and ran nothing but three print-only scripts under N/u4f-r3/r2/: p3_jumps.py, r31_te_check.py and r31_te_sums.py.

**1. Status of my round-1 findings**
- **Fixed in full (12):**
  - TE3-2: 2.4 item 2 :331-333 and item 6 :348-363; 2.6 :425-437; 2.12 :651-652; f33 :603.
  - TE3-4: 2.6 :415-437; f15 and f16 :585-586; Q11 (v) :1365-1369.
  - TE3-5: f16; 9.1 :1166.
  - TE3-6: 2.6 :444; f37; 5.1 :852-854.
  - TE3-8: 5.5 :959-988; Q2 (a); 12 item 13.
  - TE3-9: the P24 key is found once, at df-ruling :462; the bare words stand twice, at :313 and :462.
  - TE3-10 to TE3-15: :964-966, :553-556, D3 :1490, :333-335 with f12 (v), 7 item 4, :1314-1315. No 7-word run of his words stands outside 12 item 3.
- **Fixed in part (3):**
  - TE3-1: the fix is sound only under U4F-Q7 (b) (TE31-1).
  - TE3-3: the by-name reading has a rule that fails on a correct build (TE31-2).
  - TE3-7: there is no stop on the test step's total time, and the short scales can leave tests vacuous (TE31-5, TE31-10).

**2. The two Highs, checked for soundness**
- **TE3-1 (missing inputs at P3):**
  - On-time share (at least 99.9 %): reachable. With a command for every stamp, each command is resent every step until it is acknowledged. A margin of about 2 ticks gives about 0.0125 % late, within the lead bound and option B's 9. Options A and B read the same, by stamp, and W does not change it.
  - Missing share (at most 0.1 %): met under Q7 (b), not under Q7 (a). Under (a), my P3 model (which reproduces U4r's 18-20 % of steps without a command) shows the newest tick jumping 3 or more ticks in 1.16 % of steps. The words "leaves the stamps between unused" then leave 1.22 % of ticks without a stamp.
  - f36 can fail as worded, and under (a) it would stop the build. Carrying the owed stamps forward at 2 a step leaves none unused: the backlog never exceeds 3.
- **TE3-2 (forged commands):** on a correct build every kind's rule passes, and every bite fails it. I traced kinds 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6, kind 3, kind 7 and kind 10, and the twins keep the sequence numbers the state hash reads (sim/src/world.rs:1979, :1995-2009). Only wording gaps remain (TE31-11).

**3. The new items**
- **(a) The join anchor:** as built, no honest bots command can be stamped at or before the join tick. But the controller rule drops the "none until a snapshot" clause, and the endpoint still stamps 0 before a snapshot (client/src/lib.rs:429). f13 (iii) also lacks the boundary cases (TE31-4).
- **(b) The past window W:** resent copies never reach it, and no P3 loss pattern does either. The judged 200 ms lag switch and p13 are unchanged. p19 changes: its oldest 3-4 commands are dropped as late, and the input bucket of 8 datagrams already keeps the catch-up cap from acting, so "the cap refuses the excess, max 8" cannot hold (TE31-3). p20 cannot show W's size, because every command of its episode is dropped (TE31-6).
- **(c) 5.3 read by name:** each named check does fail on its bitten run and pass on its clean partner, and the list of checks that fail by length is complete for the count checks. But 5.3 has no twin runs, so the forged and clamp twin checks come out as gaps that make the run invalid. p1's new "twin check passing" therefore cannot be met, and the p9 and p12 bites also fail a second check (TE31-2).
- **(d) The rest:**
  - f38 and p21 are sound.
  - f36, f37 and the scale rule need small fixes (TE31-10).
  - f16 and f29 can pass at their short scale without exercising their claim (TE31-5).
  - Against today's disk reading (5,468 MiB free), the room after the u4r-P3 pack is about 1,752 MiB, not 1,798. KL-U4F's GB figures are off, and C62H-BOUND's two closed set folders are in no list (TE31-8).

**4. Counts and consistency**
- The counts hold:
  - tests +107 in the measured build (2.10's table sums to 107) and +122 in the bites build;
  - 63 negative cases;
  - 15 short pre-runs, with the conditional +4, +1 and +1;
  - 18 questions, 50 recheck rows and 19 open items.
- Broken:
  - 12 item 4 still says "Q1 to Q17" (TE31-9).
  - The "allowance after an idle" wording in the draft for Mustafa misstates what the checks allow (TE31-7).
  - -21's disk figure is off by 0.4 MiB (a nit).
